jurisdiction.name: Jamaica
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Jamaica has no AI law and no adopted AI strategy. Its AI governance rests on the 2025 policy recommendations of the National AI Task Force, published by the Office of the Prime Minister; the Data Protection Act 2020, whose right over automated decision-taking has applied since December 2023; and the Chief Justice's 2025 practice direction on the use of generative AI in court proceedings. A National AI Policy and an AI legislative framework are being drafted under the Office of the Prime Minister.
lead_institutions: Supreme Court of Judicature of Jamaica
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from documents read in full on official sites. The Jamaica Gazette has no online search. Not yet verified from the official text: laws on the Ministry of Justice laws portal. The draft National AI Policy, a 2026 cybercrime amendment covering generated intimate images and a planned public-sector AI literacy directive are tracked as leads.

instruments.english_title: National Artificial Intelligence - Policy Recommendations (National AI Task Force report)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Artificial Intelligence Task Force, Office of the Prime Minister
instruments.current_status: Published by the Office of the Prime Minister on 13 February 2025 as recommendations delivered in September 2024, which Cabinet was reviewing; they are recommendations, not an adopted policy. A reconstituted Task Force (first met 19 February 2026) is drafting the National AI Policy (target November 2026) and an AI legislative framework within 12 months.
instruments.summary: Report of the National AI Task Force to the Office of the Prime Minister laying the evidence base for a National AI Policy aligned with Vision 2030. After a SWOT analysis of AI use in Jamaica it sets SMART recommendations in nine areas (AI for innovation and growth, education and workforce, public awareness, infrastructure, international cooperation, legal and regulatory frameworks, government-industry collaboration, ethical foundations and a cohesive AI framework) and a phased action plan. On regulation it recommends interim guidelines for AI ethics and data privacy that keep AI applications within existing data protection law, and review of existing legislation or new legislation to facilitate AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main national AI policy document to date; the basis for the National AI Policy now being drafted.

instruments.current_status: Act No. 7 of 2020, assented to by the Governor-General on 10 July 2020. Commenced in stages by notices in the Jamaica Gazette: sections 2, 4, 56, 57, 60, 66, 74, 77 and the First Schedule from 1 December 2021 (Appointed Day Notice, 2021, Gazette 30 November 2021); sections 1 and 3, Part II (data-subject rights including section 12 on automated decision-taking) and most remaining provisions from 1 December 2023 (Additional Specified Provisions Appointed Day Notice, 2023, Gazette 1 December 2023). The OIC also publishes the 2024 registration, Minister's and disposal regulations.
instruments.summary: Jamaica's general data protection law, administered by the Information Commissioner, setting data protection standards, controller registration and data-subject rights. Section 12 lets an individual require by written notice that no decision significantly affecting them is based solely on automated processing of personal data to evaluate matters such as work performance, creditworthiness, reliability or conduct; where no notice was given the controller must inform the individual, who may within 30 days require reconsideration or a new decision not based solely on such processing, and the Commissioner can order this.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Governs personal-data processing in AI training and use and contains the country's only statutory rule on solely automated decisions.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): assented Act No. 7 of 2020 PDF read from the OIC's 'The Data Protection Act' page (pdftotext plus page-1 image showing assent of 10 July 2020); section 12 text read; commencement read from the Appointed Day Notices 2021 (text) and 2023 (scanned Gazette pages, read as images) on oic.gov.jm

instruments.official_title: Practice Direction No. 1 of 2025 – Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Court Proceedings
instruments.english_title: Practice Direction No. 1 of 2025 – Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Court Proceedings
instruments.issuing_authority: Chief Justice of Jamaica (Supreme Court of Judicature of Jamaica)
instruments.current_status: Dated and in effect from 17 September 2025; remains in force until varied or revoked and is subject to periodic review. Listed on the Supreme Court's practice directions page.
instruments.summary: Practice direction issued by the Chief Justice for proceedings in the Supreme Court, the Revenue Court and the High Court and Circuit Court Divisions of the Gun Court, governing the use of generative AI by attorneys, parties, self-represented litigants and others. It requires GenAI-assisted court documents to be verified and free of fabricated authorities and prohibits GenAI for affidavits, witness statements, expert evidence, evidence, purported originals, unapproved images and likeness avatars in virtual hearings. Documents prepared with GenAI must carry a declaration in the appended form, and non-compliance can lead to exclusion, costs, contempt or referral to the General Legal Council.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First binding rules on generative AI use issued by a Jamaican public body.
instruments.publisher_name: Supreme Court of Judicature of Jamaica
instruments.scope: Jamaica (national): Supreme Court, Revenue Court and Gun Court divisions

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: National sources in Jamaica were searched, including Parliament, the Office of the Prime Minister, ministries, the judiciary and regulators. No qualifying material was found for risk and assurance, public-sector AI, procurement, cyber-security, standards, sandboxes, readiness indexes, drafts, international instruments or historical documents. The official gazette has no online search, so the official text of the Cybercrimes (Amendment) Act 2026 and whether consultation on the National AI Policy began in September 2026 remain to be checked.

Practice Direction No. 1 of 2025 recorded administrative_policy_mandatory_in_scope (binds court users). BOJ standards (2024, 2025) mention AI in passing (leads). Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: japarliament.gov.jm and OIC-hosted Act/Gazette notices: Data Protection Act 2020 (s.12 automated decisions) recorded; no AI-specific law; Cybercrimes (Amendment) Act 2026 (deepfake intimate images) held as lead (no official text found); laws.moj.gov.jm unreachable (curl TLS failure, WebFetch 503). Jamaica Gazette not searchable online beyond notices hosted by OIC.; Government: OPM (National AI Task Force recommendations recorded; draft National AI Policy, AI literacy directive and UNESCO RAM as leads). No national AI strategy adopted; no public-sector AI/GenAI guideline or procurement rules found.; Ministries: Searched education, health, justice, finance: nothing found beyond press statements (MOEY AI tool pilots; MOF statement on AI in auditing). BOJ: only passing AI mentions in governance and cyber standards (leads). FSC, OUR, Broadcasting Commission, JAMPRO: searched, nothing AI-specific found. No national cyber authority AI guidance found. leads.title: The Cybercrimes (Amendment) Act, 2026
leads.note: Passed House 3 February 2026 and Senate 1 May 2026 (JIS). Per government statements it redefines intimate images to include content 'generated or created' (covering AI deepfakes) and creates an offence of publishing them without consent; the Act does not name AI. No official text, assent or commencement found on japarliament.gov.jm or the MOJ laws portal (TLS failure). Record once official text is located.
